questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go somewhere with interesting courses available. And I also chose Berlin because I have family in Germany and wanted to practise the language more.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really good experience overall!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is always quite stressful and confusing to manage communication between different institutions in different countries. The platforms and information available are helpful, but I have the feeling that there is always something that remains complicated. I met up with another student from KU on my own initiative, who had been on exchange at Freie as well and asked her a bunch of questions. This was really calming and helpful, because she gave me some insiders tips on how to cope with the German and Danish systems, and told me that everything will work out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of assistance available from Freie's Erasmus team. Well prepared and planned.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is really hard to find a place to live in Berlin! Not just for incoming students, but for everyone! I found my room through Instagram, but it was pure luck.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved living off Campus in Neukölln. Berlin is wonderful, but Freie is placed quite far out of the centre, so I would rather recommend searching for somewhere in the city center instead.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Can't say anything about it, since I found housing on my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As the German semesters are very differently structured than the Danish ones, I decided to move to Berlin in February even though my courses didn't begin until mid-April. So when registration started, I had already visited Freie and picked up my studentcard and so on in my own slow pace. Otherwise, registration was just meeting up for the introduction day and the first week of courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of orientation and information available from the Erasmus team. I found it confusing that the German uni system makes it possible for you to try out different courses in the first couple of weeks of the semester, before you finally decide. This is really great, but not very easy to navigate as an Erasmus student, who has to live up to some very strict demands from your home university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly successful, although I wasn't allowed to take a course I really wanted to join at Freie, because KU wouldn't allow me as a masters student to participate in a course with mixed bachelors and mastersstudents present...

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses in the first week and see what you like. Also, don't be scared to supply with courses from other universities in Berlin. I took two courses at Freie and two at Humbolt, even though I was only enrolled at Freie. In Germany you can always write directly to the professors and ask whether you are allowed to participate in their courses. This makes everything really nice and personal. Though, also gives you a lot of paper-work and deadlines to remember. But things will work out if you organize well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high and I found most course at Freie really innovative in their approaches.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had two seminars at Freie with around 20-30 people in each, this made it a really great room for discussions and participation. I loved to be very engaged as a student. I also had one course with two professors present at ever seminar, one from the philosophy department and one from comparative literature. This sparked some super interesting discussions and elaborations among the professors themselves.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Humanismen, Humus, Feminismen
The face: an approach from many angles
Fictions of Addiction 
Dis/entangling material futures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The face: an approach from many angles was conducted by a visiting professor from NYU, she had a really interesting approach.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My bag got stolen, I did not have an insurance, and I had to replace a lot of things... Also: clubbing is expensive!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and coffee at cafés are nice and affordable, compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Berlin is full of museums, clubs, shops and more. I went to lots of really great events and concerts.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus team organized a lot of social stuff and sports activities, I never went. Found things on my own.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find some kind of hobby or sport to do in town, its a really nice way to spend time with other people and maybe get new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to the Bauhaus museums one day in Dessau and spent the whole day, really great. Also: take the trains out of the city and go hiking or swim in the lakes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me, since I have German family.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone takes the train to and from campus at Freie, so you quickly become friends with people from your classes when you walk to and from the train together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not very many. Maybe all the paperwork, because a lot of stuff still isn't digitalized in Germany.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All the ecological and vegan opportunities. Also: people in Berlin are very open and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember to enjoy the city and the culture and not spend all your time studying 
2) Its tough to be alone in the beginning, but things will change slowly, and you will start to feel really at home, so if you have the chance to go early or stay longer before or after the semester, do it. 
3) Choose courses with professors that inspire you or whose approach you like

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that you can take courses outside of Freie as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends and attending nice events!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely in the beginning, because the fact is: when you move to another city, no-one knows you. But slowly people will. Be open and have patience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
